A good protag, huh? Time for an attempted answer with Deadly Premonition, GTA IV, and Heavy Rain as examples, and I'll spoiler tag what I would regard as a spoiler, but you've been warned.

I'd say the important 4 are: Competence (that they can actually do their job), Motive (why they're doing what they are), Further development (to reveal more etc) and a flaw (either something we can relate to, or at least not make them overly powerful).

Competence

  • Deadly Premonition has so much eccentricity, yet York still manages to keep things cool, and tries to always do the right thing.
  • GTA IV - it's clear from dialogue etc Niko wants to escape his past, and tries his hardest to do so. But it's always just out of reach.
  • Heavy Rain - even though you're following essentially four storylines, each overlapping a bit, they all are doing what they can to try and find the missing child. The FBI agent does what he can through mostly legal channels, the journalist follows sketchy leads, the father plays the emotional scapegoat (as in, he's the most invested by default given he's the father so when he's around it's mostly where the feels come in), and a PI also follows some equally sketchy leads.

Motive or Goals

  • In DP it's clear York has been tailing a serial killer across the US. It's also quite clear cut - there's a baddie on the loose. Everybody can easily understand that.
  • GTA IV's Niko, whilst clearly more action packed because it's GTA, it's not hard for us to see that all he wants is a better life. Sure, he's killed people previously, entered the US illegally, and kills a few more, but his ultimate aim is a better life, and to move on from his past.
  • Heavy Rain is also fairly clear cut: each of them are trying to find a missing child, whilst exhausting what leads they have to find out just what's happened.

Further development over the game.

  • DP York , but also learns more about the townsfolk, etc. Just like us to the game, York is an outsider to the town, which makes him more relatable. We're also more intrigued because it's a detective tale, so we get to be with York as the plot unravels, slowly but surely.
  • GTA IV As I said earlier, Niko is more action packed because he's living in GTA. However, we still get the heart to heart cutscenes as to his thoughts on America, his cousin Roman, and all the rest of it.
  • Heavy Rain There's character development in all of the main cast, some of which you have control over.

They have to have a flaw

  • DP Kinda hard to pinpoint, but I'd say York is flawed in his approach. He's calm and collective when he wants to be, but he can equally just be off the walls crazy and slightly clueless.
  • GTA IV Trouble just tends to follow in his wake. Again, he plays nice when he wants to be, but he very easily just stirs shit up and dials it to 11.
  • Heavy Rain

There's other things you can do, like having a silent protagonist to make the player feel more like it is them, but it's not like you can't achieve the same if the main character is voiced.
